title: Zhuangzi woke up unsure if he was a man or a dreaming butterfly
body: In a famous passage of the Zhuangzi, a Daoist classic from China’s Warring States period, Zhuang Zhou dreams he is a butterfly, fluttering happily with no idea who he is. On waking, he cannot tell whether he is a man who dreamt of a butterfly or a butterfly now dreaming it is a man. He calls this ‘the transformation of things’, a playful challenge to fixed identities, written long before Descartes worried about dreams.
